A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sparse polynomial optimization approach to BNN verification. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and added experiments.

before.justification: V1 reports original MNIST robustness-verification results, solver runtimes, and synthetic-network comparisons in Section 5 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: V2 retains original verification results and reports additional synthetic-network and CIFAR-10 experiments, including Table 8.

M1.justification: The sign-function encoding, redundant quadratic constraints, tightened first-order SDP relaxation, and sparse variable grouping remain unchanged in Sections 2–4 and Appendix A.4. Larger-network evaluations do not introduce a new verification procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds CIFAR-10 robustness verification, extending evaluation from MNIST handwritten digits to natural color images (Appendix B, Table 8). MNIST and both existing perturbation norms remain; larger synthetic network configurations do not themselves constitute new dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 replaces the explicitly LP-augmented QCQP+LP comparator with a reported QCQP comparator, whose bounds sometimes fall below LP. The LP and main Soft-MILP/Soft-MINP comparisons remain. Newly cited general verification methods are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: V2 adds runtime averages over instances certified by SDP and replaces the small synthetic configurations with much larger dense and explicitly row-sparse networks. The new CIFAR-10 protocol uses BNN3 [3072,5000,800,10], 22 correctly classified images among the first 40, and a 3600-second limit. Existing MNIST configurations and 600-second limits remain.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 substantially expands the synthetic comparison into a study of bound quality and scalability across network sizes, depths, and row sparsities, while dropping the previous QCQP+LP control. Appendix B also adds concrete CIFAR-10 cases where SDP certifies robustness or remains inconclusive while MILP finds attacks.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or error bars. The new parenthetical entries in Tables 1–2 are average runtimes over certified instances, not uncertainty estimates. The 10,000-point random sampling procedure already appears in v1.

E6.justification: The original MNIST certification counts and overall runtimes remain, with additional subset runtimes in v2. Table 3 replaces nine small-network rows with 26 new configurations; Table 8 adds 22 CIFAR-10 cases, with four SDP robustness certificates versus one from Soft-MILP. Table 4 removes image 83 at delta-infinity 1.75. These are added or replaced results, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 corrects the definition of nv(A) for a p-by-q matrix from a q-dimensional vector in v1 Section 3 to a p-dimensional vector in Section 1.3, consistent with its row norms. The principal theorems and appendix proofs retain their substance; the additional inequality in Appendix A.3 restates an existing conclusion.

C1.justification: The methodological and novelty claims remain. Section 1.1 replaces the broad over-20-fold speed claim with reported averages of 4.5-fold for infinity-norm and 11.4-fold for 2-norm verification, plus over-50-fold in some severe cases. The conclusion removes the projected average 20-fold acceleration from embedding SDP bounds in exact solvers.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of larger-network scalability and acknowledges CIFAR-10 cases where SDP is inconclusive but MILP efficiently establishes non-robustness, attributing this difference to feasibility search. Existing interior-point solver limitations and the proposed integration with branch-and-bound remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds the hardware used for the revised Table 3 experiments: a 26-core Xeon Gold 6348 server with 756 GB RAM, qualifying the existing desktop description. The established training and solver details remain, and the reformatted repository link points to the same code location.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 adds a general-verification overview covering bound propagation, NNV 2.0, PyRAT, Marabou, and sampling-based approaches. V2 also adds references on on-device BNN applications and training. The central positioning relative to BNN verification and SDP methods, including the novelty claim, remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The section sequence and most prose remain. V2 expands introductory examples and explanations, replaces much clique terminology with subsets of decision variables, renames Appendix A.4, and updates author and publication text. Editing is localized rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite; Table 7's caption loses a numerical multiplier and becomes incomplete.

P2.justification: V2 adopts ICLR typography and headers while retaining the single-column organization. Figure 1 receives revised labels and an expanded caption; Figure 2 changes colors and legend order. Table 2 becomes vertically stacked, Table 3 reorganizes its columns, and Table 8 is added.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the empirical argument more informative through timing summaries on the same certified instances, larger-network and CIFAR-10 tests, and explicit discussion of cases favoring MILP. Removing the projected 20-fold acceleration of exact solvers also reduces overstatement. The gains are limited by the small CIFAR-10 evaluation and the loss of the explicitly documented QCQP+LP control; the core method and proofs remain essentially unchanged.
